10 A nitrogen molecule P travelling at a speed of 320 m s–1 in a vacuum collides with a stationary
nitrogen molecule Q.
After the collision, P travels at a velocity of 180 m s–1 at an angle of 55 to its original path.
Q travels in a direction at an angle of 34 to the initial path of P.

Assume that there are no external forces acting on the molecules.
What is the magnitude v of the velocity of Q after the collision?
A

hints: Notice the before diagram has all motion along one line at $320 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, while after the collision P has $180 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ at $55^{\circ}$ above that line and Q has $v$ at $34^{\circ}$ below it.
Connect no external forces to conservation of vector momentum, and resolve along the original path so only $\cos55^{\circ}$ and $\cos34^{\circ}$ components count.
Set $m \times 320 = m \times 180\cos55^{\circ} + m \times v\cos34^{\circ}$, cancel the equal nitrogen mass $m$, then solve for $v$.
walkthrough: Take the $x$-axis along the initial path of P. Before collision total $x$-momentum is $m_P \times 320 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ because Q is stationary.
After collision, resolve each velocity along $x$. P contributes $180\cos55^{\circ}$ and Q contributes $v\cos34^{\circ}$, both in $\text{m s}^{-1}$.
Conservation of $x$-momentum with equal masses $m_P = m_Q = m$ gives $m \times 320 = m \times 180\cos55^{\circ} + m \times v\cos34^{\circ}$, so $320 = 180\cos55^{\circ} + v\cos34^{\circ}$.
Substitute $\cos55^{\circ} \approx 0.574$ and $\cos34^{\circ} \approx 0.829$. Then $180\cos55^{\circ} \approx 103.2 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $v \times 0.829 \approx 320 - 103.2 = 216.8$.
Hence $v \approx 216.8 / 0.829 \approx 262 \text{ m s}^{-1}$, closest to $260 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ with correct unit. This is option D

A.explanation: Too small because it does not conserve the $x$-component of momentum along the original $320 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ path.

B.explanation: Too small because $180\cos55^{\circ} + 140\cos34^{\circ}$ is less than $320 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ in the initial direction.

C.explanation: Incorrectly assumes symmetry with P, ignoring that $55^{\circ}$ and $34^{\circ}$ give different $x$-components.

D.explanation: Satisfies $320 = 180\cos55^{\circ} + v\cos34^{\circ}$, giving $v$ about $260 \text{ m s}^{-1}$.
